checked.description: Whether the setting is on. Bound to the control BOTH ways, and the two halves do different jobs. The PROPERTY is what keeps tracking: once the reader flips the box the checkedness dirty flag is set and the content attribute stops controlling the live state, so an attribute binding alone would look right until the first click and then silently stop. The ATTRIBUTE is written as well so the control's defaultChecked can never disagree with the element's state — the same shape jx-textfield ships for value. The cost is that defaultChecked is also the form-reset default, so until the element is form-associated (specs/ui.md §3.2) form.reset() moves this switch nowhere. That is the deliberate half of the trade: with no form association the element never hears the reset, so a working reset would move the CONTROL to the authored default and leave the element's checked state behind it, and a control that silently disagrees with its own element is worse than a reset that does nothing.

disabled.description: Cannot be flipped or focused. Disabled, never absent, and the hint moves from the tip to the row's title while it is: a disabled control cannot open a tip, and why the setting cannot be changed is exactly what the reader hovers to find out.

hint.description: The tooltip on the row: what turning the setting on does, or why it cannot be changed. The same hybrid jx-button and jx-action-button ship. While the switch is ENABLED it is drawn as a jx-tooltip child of this element — shown on keyboard focus at once and on hover after the tip's delay, hoverable and dismissible with Escape (SC 1.4.13) — and the control names it in aria-describedby, so it is a description beside the name and never the name itself. While the switch is DISABLED it is the native title of the wrapping label instead, because a disabled control receives no focus and no pointer event and could never open a tip, while the platform still shows a title on hover. Never both at once; empty draws neither. ONE difference from the buttons, and it is the platform's rather than the kit's: the tip is wired by `for` alone and the row declares NO `interestfor`. Interest invokers are supported on `a`, `area` and `button` only — never on a label or an input — so the attribute here would show nothing on Chrome 152 while telling the tooltip sidecar the platform had the pair, which is the one combination that draws no tip on any engine. The sidecar binds the label on every engine instead, and that is what the switch pays for a tooltip: six listeners on the row and two on the tip, always, where a button pays them only where the platform lacks the attribute.

label.description: The accessible name, forwarded to the control as aria-label. Leave it empty when the slotted text is on screen: the wrapping label is then the name, and a second one would be read twice.

labelledby.description: Forwarded to the inner control as aria-labelledby, for a visible label the element does not own.

describedby.description: Forwarded to the inner control as aria-describedby, for the help or error sentence on the row.

name.description: The form field name, forwarded to the control.

size.description: sm, md or lg. The track scales with it so a row of controls lines up.

tabindex.description: Forwarded to the inner control as its tabindex, which is what makes a roving caret possible: the focusable node is the input inside, not the host and not the label that wraps it, so a jx-toolbar moving focus writes this rather than reaching into a child's internals. It is a PROPERTY ONLY (el.tabindex = "0") and deliberately not an observed attribute: written as an attribute it would land on the host as well, and a host carrying tabindex is itself focusable, so the one control would become two tab stops.

uid.description: This row's own id stem, minted on mount by the tooltip sidecar. The label's id, the tip's id and the two attributes that wire one to the other are all built from it, so a consumer writes none of them and two hinted switches on one panel cannot collide. Empty until the mount microtask, which is why every binding that reads it guards on it.

onMount.description: Mints the id stem the hint's tooltip is wired by. A document cannot: the closed operator set has no counter and no identity.

onChange.description: Mirrors the reader's flip into checked. The native change and input events bubble from the control as they always do, so a host reads e.target.checked exactly as it would from a bare input.

& [part=\"input\"].transition: background var(--jx-dur-1) var(--jx-ease-out), border-color var(--jx-dur-1) var(--jx-ease-out)
